rv.q: Pulitzer Prize winner burns bright enough to scorch but also to illuminate.
It’s well acted, stylishly presented and very nicely, erm, tackled: preferred over 9 out of 10 Cats, you might say.
Sienna Miller as Maggie provides exactly that in the first half, bursting into the bedroom she shares with her husband, Brick.
She is a reasonable but hardly first-rate actress.
Miller turns in a faultless performance.
That said, the scene between Meaney and O’Connell is a cut above – some welcome warm blood in a production that never quite clicks.

cn.t: Miller sizzles in this uneven but often thrilling revival that burns brightest in its first half, though the production doesn't always sustain Williams's dramatic flame across all three acts.
